meta.title: International Relations Demographic Database (1950–2075)
meta.sources: United Nations Population Division (WPP 2024 Revision) & US Census International Data Base (IDB)
meta.description: Age-sex cohort structure, dependency ratios, and median age trajectories for major powers and strategic regional actors.

United States.irStrategicNote: Maintains demographic vitality through sustained international immigration, offsetting sub-replacement native fertility and preserving a stable working-age defense base.

China.irStrategicNote: The One-Child Policy (1979-2015) accelerated one of the fastest demographic aging shifts in world history. China is growing old before it grows rich, with working-age population already contracting.

India.irStrategicNote: Surpassed China as the world most populous country in 2023. Enjoys a prolonged demographic dividend with hundreds of millions entering prime working age through 2045.

Russia.irStrategicNote: Marked by the post-WWII male deficit, the catastrophic 1990s post-Soviet mortality spike and birth trough, and ongoing war casualties, constraining long-term power projection.

Japan.irStrategicNote: Pioneer of the super-aged society. Nearly 30% of its population is over 65, creating severe defense recruitment constraints and debt-servicing pressures.

Germany.irStrategicNote: Europe economic engine faces acute labor shortfalls as the baby boom generation retires, driving high dependency ratios despite substantial immigration.

Nigeria.irStrategicNote: Classic youthful expansive pyramid with a massive youth bulge. Projected to become the third most populous nation on Earth by 2050, reshaping African regional hegemony.

South Korea.irStrategicNote: World lowest fertility rate (~0.72). Facing an unprecedented peacetime demographic contraction with profound implications for military conscription against North Korea.
